key_insight: A neural surrogate of NGSpice helps fit transistor-model parameters to measurements at 77 K, aiming to make cryogenic SKY130 devices usable in standard circuit simulations.
problem_solved: Cryogenic circuit design needs compact transistor models that capture measured low-temperature behavior while remaining compatible with standard simulators.
method: Fit BSIM4 compact-model parameters to measured current–voltage curves from SKY130 transistors at 77 K.
Use a neural surrogate that maps model parameters and device geometry to output and transfer characteristics.
Perform bounded least-squares parameter extraction, supported by a bank of NGSpice simulations.
impact: This illustrates how ML surrogates can support physics-based model calibration for semiconductor design. For AI/ML practitioners, it offers an application of learned simulation models beyond conventional prediction tasks; the supplied abstract does not report quantitative performance gains.
visual_elements: Workflow diagram: NGSpice simulations → neural surrogate → parameter fitting → calibrated BSIM4 model.
Transistor icon paired with a thermometer marking 77 K.
Input–output schematic showing model parameters and device geometry mapped to electrical characteristics.
paper_title: Surrogate-Assisted Compact-Model Extraction for SKY130 CMOS at 77 K
paper_authors: Aaron Wang, Olivia Gzamouranis, Vaibhav Lohia, Hershel Fei Xun Weiner, Olivia Seidel
